question.prompt: The lengths in inches of the three sides of each of four triangles \(\mathrm{I},\) \(\mathrm{II},\) \(\mathrm{III},\) and \(\mathrm{IV}\) are as follows: \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}\quad&3,4,5\\ \mathrm{II}\quad&4,7\frac12,8\frac12\\ \mathrm{III}\quad&7,24,25\\ \mathrm{IV}\quad&3\frac12,4\frac12,5\frac12 \end{aligned} \] Of these four given triangles, the only right triangles are:

solutions.explanation:
For a triangle whose longest side is \(c\), the Pythagorean theorem and its converse say that it is right exactly when the other two sides satisfy \(a^2+b^2=c^2\). Testing each triangle gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{I}:\quad&3^2+4^2=25=5^2,\\
\mathrm{II}:\quad&4^2+7.5^2=72.25=8.5^2,\\
\mathrm{III}:\quad&7^2+24^2=625=25^2,\\
\mathrm{IV}:\quad&3.5^2+4.5^2=32.5\ne30.25=5.5^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus exactly triangles \(\mathrm{I}\), \(\mathrm{II}\), and \(\mathrm{III}\) are right triangles, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Test the longest side
